snowglobe.handbook.page.1:
§lThe Globe Keeper's Handbook§r


Notes on worlds kept under glass, by Odile, glassblower of the northern pass.

§o(Read on, and look after them.)
snowglobe.handbook.page.2:
My grandmother said every snow globe holds a real winter, very far away and very small.

She was half right. They aren't far away at all.

Hold one close, crouch low, and press your eye to the glass...
snowglobe.handbook.page.3:
...and you'll be standing inside.

The glass becomes your sky. The room you left becomes a land of giants: your own house, a hundred times over, with whoever's at home peering in at you.
snowglobe.handbook.page.4:
§lMaking globes§r

All are glass around something, on a base:

§8Snow globe§r: snow, planks below
§8Terrarium§r: moss
§8Storm globe§r: lightning rod, on copper and deepslate
§8Ship in a bottle§r: a boat and a log
snowglobe.handbook.page.5:
§8Desert globe§r: a dead bush, on cut sandstone
§8Aquarium§r: kelp, on dark prismarine
§8Star globe§r: a spyglass, on blackstone and amethyst
§8Nether jar§r: a magma block, with a blackstone lid
snowglobe.handbook.page.6:
§lHandling§r

§8Right-click§r the glass to shake it.
§8Sneak + right-click§r to step inside.
§8Right-click the base§r to turn it.
§8Punch§r the glass to knock: anyone inside will hear it, loud.
snowglobe.handbook.page.7:
§lInside§r

Build as you would anywhere. A new globe is empty: bring what you'll build with. Nothing inside is made from nothing, and nothing is lost.

To leave, right-click the glass wall with an empty hand.
snowglobe.handbook.page.8:
§lSeasons§r

Shake a snow globe and the year turns: winter, spring, summer, autumn.

Shaken into winter, real snow settles on everything inside. Shaken into spring, it melts away.
snowglobe.handbook.page.9:
§lSkies§r

Every globe has a sky of its own: blue over the snow, an endless sunset over the dunes, night in the star globe, storm grey, deep water blue in the aquarium, and red in the nether jar.

The light inside follows it.
snowglobe.handbook.page.10:
§lCompany§r

Animals on a lead come in with you.

Fish go in from their bucket, into the globe's water (there must be some). A water bucket catches one back out.
snowglobe.handbook.page.11:
§lMusic boxes§r

Press a note block into a globe's base and it becomes a music box. Each turn of the base winds it, and it plays the globe's own tune until it runs down.
snowglobe.handbook.page.12:
§lBigger worlds§r

A Create schematic, right-clicked onto an empty globe, is built inside it, and the globe grows to fit. In survival, you pay for every block.

Big globes look big, too.
snowglobe.handbook.page.13:
§lGlobes in globes§r

A globe can stand inside another, and you can go in deeper still. Leaving takes you out one glass at a time.

A §8collector's shelf§r shows two globes, and keeps up with what's built in them.
snowglobe.handbook.page.14:
Keep them out of the sun, and dust them now and then.

And if you ever hear a knock from inside one of yours, it's only polite to knock back.

§o- O.
